subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Flavor Wheel
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Flavor Wheel.

hook.text: The SCA Coffee Taster's Flavor Wheel maps coffee into categories: fruity, nutty, sweet, floral, and more.

buildup.text: The wheel was created by sensory scientists in 2016 using data from thousands of professional tasting sessions.

discovery.text: Coffee contains over 1,000 aromatic compounds—more than wine. The wheel helps tasters name what they sense.

twist.text: Tasting descriptors like 'blueberry' don't mean blueberry was added. The same chemical compounds are present.

climax.text: Training your palate with the flavor wheel turns vague 'good coffee' into specific, repeatable preferences.

punchline.text: Over 1,000 aroma compounds. The wheel helps you name them.

quiz.question: How many aromatic compounds does coffee contain?

details.summary: The coffee flavor wheel, created by the Specialty Coffee Association, maps the taste vocabulary for coffee from broad categories like fruity and nutty to specific descriptors like blueberry or hazelnut. It is the industry standard for communicating about flavor objectively and consistently.
details.whyItMatters: A shared flavor vocabulary allows roasters, buyers, and farmers to communicate precisely about coffee quality, improving trade and consumer education.
takeaways: The SCA flavor wheel is the industry standard for coffee tasting
It maps flavors from broad categories to specific descriptors
Cupping protocols use the wheel for objective evaluation

faq.question: How do you use the coffee flavor wheel?
faq.answer: Start at the center with broad categories like fruity, sweet, or nutty. Move outward to narrow the descriptor. If you taste something fruity, ask whether it is berry-like, citrus, or stone fruit. The wheel trains your palate to be specific.

faq.question: Who created the coffee flavor wheel?
faq.answer: The Specialty Coffee Association published the current version in 2016, based on research by World Coffee Research. It updated an earlier 1995 version and was developed through large-scale sensory analysis with trained tasters from around the world.
